objects.name: Analytic 2139
objects.description: Real-time monitoring identifies rapid, bulk deletion of files across Industrial Control System (ICS) data directories on a Linux asset, by a User Identifier (UID) not associated with documented data retention management, correlated with worm-based propagation indicators consistent with documented Linux wiper malware (Awfulshred, SoloShred). OT operational-fidelity gate: Alert only when the action is not attributable to an authorized operator/engineering source for the specific target and function, and it is either outside an approved change/maintenance window or lacks matching change-control context; where telemetry permits, require corroborating device, configuration, or process-state effect. Suppress activity that fully matches approved maintenance, commissioning, failover, recovery, or tested control procedures.

x_mitre_log_source_references.name: auditd:SYSCALL+PATH
x_mitre_log_source_references.channel: Linux Audit SYSCALL+PATH records: rm/shred/dd operations across multiple Industrial Control Systems (ICS) data directories exceeding bulk deletion threshold, by User Identifier (UID) not in authorized data management UIDs

x_mitre_log_source_references.name: auditd:SYSCALL
x_mitre_log_source_references.channel: Linux Audit SYSCALL/EXECVE/SOCKADDR records (configured audit rule): Secure Shell (SSH)-based propagation pattern (connection to multiple hosts followed by file transfer and execution) within a short window

x_mitre_mutable_elements.description: Allowlist of backup/archival/retention management tools authorized to perform bulk file operations.
File count threshold across monitored directories that distinguishes bulk destruction from routine cleanup.
Time window over which bulk deletion activity is measured.
IP allowlist of workstations authorized to issue memory erase commands.
Time window after bulk deletion within which a system crash is considered part of the same destructive event.
